reasoning: Read both sides. src/KOKKOS/pppm_kokkos.h:439-449 declares PPPMKokkos' own k_rho_coeff/d_rho_coeff, fft1, fft2, remap and 'Grid3dKokkos<DeviceType> *gc', shadowing PPPM::gc; pppm_kokkos.cpp:105-108 nulls those shadows only. 'grep -rn reset_grid src/KOKKOS' returns nothing, so PPPM::reset_grid() (src/KSPACE/pppm.cpp:637-668, declared 'void reset_grid() override' at pppm.h:35) is inherited unchanged and is reached from src/fix_balance.cpp:341 'if (force->kspace) force->kspace->reset_grid();'. Inside PPPM::reset_grid, unqualified 'gc' binds to PPPM::gc, which is set to nullptr in the PPPM constructor and never re-assigned in a KOKKOS run (PPPMKokkos::allocate assigns only its own shadowing gc, pppm_kokkos.cpp:797). That deref is guarded by '!overlap_allowed' (default overlap_allowed = 1, src/kspace.cpp:55), so it only bites with 'kspace_modify overlap no'. The unguarded crash is one line later: compute_rho_coeff() is NOT virtual (src/KSPACE/pppm.h:142), so PPPM::compute_rho_coeff runs and writes 'rho_coeff[l][m] = a[l][k]; ... drho_coeff[l-1][m] = l*a[l][k];' while PPPM::rho_coeff/drho_coeff are nullptr ('rho1d = rho_coeff = drho1d = drho_coeff = nullptr;' pppm.cpp:122) because PPPMKokkos::allocate (pppm_kokkos.cpp:791-892) creates only k_rho_coeff/d_rho_coeff and never memory->create2d_offset(rho_coeff,...) the way PPPM::allocate does at pppm.cpp:913-914. Even setting the crash aside, the freshly re-created k_rho_coeff would be left uninitialized: PPPMKokkos::compute_rho_coeff() + k_rho_coeff.modify_host()/sync is only called from PPPMKokkos::init().
fix: Add 'void reset_grid() override;' to PPPMKokkos and implement it as a copy of PPPM::reset_grid that uses the KOKKOS members: deallocate(); if (peratom_allocate_flag) deallocate_peratom(); set_grid_local(); allocate(); if (!overlap_allowed && !gc->ghost_adjacent()) error->all(...) (with gc now the Grid3dKokkos); compute_gf_denom(); compute_rho_coeff(); k_rho_coeff.template modify<LMPHostType>(); k_rho_coeff.template sync<DeviceType>(); setup(). (Alternative: make PPPM::compute_rho_coeff virtual and drop the gc shadowing.)

Read PPPMKokkos::init (pppm_kokkos.cpp:139-300) in full: it contains no reference to slab_auto or auto_slab_volfactor; it runs the single 'while (order >= minorder)' loop (:221-250) and then 'if (!gewaldflag) adjust_gewald();' with no outer convergence loop. The CPU base does both: src/KSPACE/pppm.cpp:295-298 sets slab_volfactor = auto_slab_volfactor(...) before the order loop, and :354-366 re-derives it after adjust_gewald() and iterates (up to 5 times, erroring out if it does not converge), then prints 'auto slab volfactor' (:394-397). src/kspace.cpp:523-530 accepts 'kspace_modify slab auto' for any style with pppmflag set (PPPMKokkos inherits pppmflag=1 from PPPM) and leaves slab_volfactor = 1.0 for init() to fix; nothing in PPPMKokkos::init rejects it. With slab_volfactor stuck at 1.0, zprd_slab == zprd, gc->set_zfactor(1.0) inserts no vacuum, and slabcorr() still applies the EW3DC dipole correction because slabflag == 1 -- wrong energies/z-forces with no warning (kspace_modify's own log line at src/kspace.cpp:679 still says 'Slab volfactor is determined automatically').
fix: Preferred: port the auto loop from PPPM::init into PPPMKokkos::init -- compute 'const bool slab_auto_enabled = (slabflag == 1 && slab_auto);', call auto_slab_volfactor() before the order loop, wrap the order loop plus adjust_gewald() in the outer 'while (true)' that re-derives slab_volfactor and breaks on convergence (auto_slab_volfactor is a file-static in pppm.cpp, so it must be moved to a shared header or duplicated). Minimum acceptable: 'if (slabflag == 1 && slab_auto) error->all(FLERR,"Cannot (yet) use PPPM Kokkos with kspace_modify slab auto");' next to the existing 'diff ad' check at pppm_kokkos.cpp:145.
Replace the second 'fft1 = nullptr;' at pppm_kokkos.cpp:913 with 'fft2 = nullptr;'.

reasoning: The code is exactly as described: pppm_kokkos.cpp:906-908 'memoryKK->destroy_kokkos(d_density_fft,density_fft); memoryKK->destroy_kokkos(d_work1,work1); memoryKK->destroy_kokkos(d_work2,work2);', while allocate() creates through the DualViews (pppm_kokkos.cpp:836-843 'memoryKK->create_kokkos(k_density_fft,density_fft,nfft_both,...)' etc.) and only then takes the device handles. pppm_kokkos.h:427-432 confirms k_* are tdual_FFT_SCALAR_1d and d_* are plain t_FFT_SCALAR_1d, so the destroy calls reset only the device handle: MemoryKokkos::destroy_kokkos (src/KOKKOS/memory_kokkos.h:82-88) is just 'if (array == nullptr) return; data = TYPE(); array = nullptr;'. ADJUSTMENT: this is not a leak. The DualView is a member and releases its allocation either when the next create_kokkos() assigns over it in allocate() or when the object is destroyed, so the only real effect is that the old host+device buffers stay alive across the deallocate()/allocate() pair in init() and reset_grid(), i.e. a transient peak of roughly 2x the FFT work-array footprint. Also note the host-side pointers density_fft/work1/work2 are correctly nulled, so nothing dangles.
fix: Pass the DualViews so the allocation is actually released before the new one is made: 'memoryKK->destroy_kokkos(k_density_fft,density_fft); memoryKK->destroy_kokkos(k_work1,work1); memoryKK->destroy_kokkos(k_work2,work2);' and additionally reset the derived device handles ('d_density_fft = typename FFT_AT::t_FFT_SCALAR_1d(); ...'), since a live d_* handle would otherwise keep the device allocation alive on its own.
